![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040724/assets/cbe1a9cf99e5a3b2cae80a4bfd01cdcabdc77560ccbb17ff9c7aa580a532d114.png)

The semi-ellipse above is defined by the parametric equations 

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

What is the domain of the parameter $\theta ?$
worked_solution:
The parametric equations of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ are

$$
x=a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

In our case, $a=2$ and $b=4.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the *full* ellipse are

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a semi-ellipse, we associate the parameter $\theta $ with the central angle formed by a point $(x,y)$ on the elipse and the $x$-axis. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040724/assets/5d615d9fd29a09345b05ee4d80ffdc49198924d0cd44edb9c815270543fae60f.png)

We can see that if we restrict $\theta $ to $[0,\pi ]$, we get the semi-ellipse.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the semi-ellipse are 

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,\pi ].
$$
